statement: You are given an integer n ≥ 2.
n is prime if its only positive divisors are 1 and n itself. Checking divisors up to √n is enough, since any larger divisor pairs with a smaller one.
Decide whether n is prime. The visualizer reports the result as PRIME or NOT PRIME.

examples.explanation: No integer from 2 to 5 (the integer part of √29) divides 29, so its only divisors are 1 and 29.
100 has nine divisors, 2, 4, 5 and 10 among them, so it is not prime.
2 is divisible only by 1 and 2. It is the smallest prime.
